text:
Colorado arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 5-2 win in Chicago in which the Avalanche came back from two goals down. They've won three straight and are without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. Columbus has been idle since a 3-1 loss in Dallas and is 2-3-0 in its last five, outscored 16-11. The story is Valeri Nichushkin, who faces his old team for the first time after 404 games in Colorado colors. That isn't in our numbers, so we won't pretend it decides anything.

Our model has Colorado ahead in chance quality, with 54% of the expected goals at five on five against Columbus's 48%, and a 3.3 to 2.76 edge in expected goals tonight. The Avalanche's results (a +19 goal difference) are running ahead of their chances, so finishing is doing much of the lifting. Both power plays and penalty kills are close to even. In net, projected starters Scott Wedgewood (COL) and Jet Greaves (CBJ) both sit slightly below expected this season, though each was well above it last year.

Nathan MacKinnon is 40% to score and 83% for a point, riding a five-game point streak. Artturi Lehkonen has 13 points in his last ten games and the chances to back it up. For Columbus, Adam Fantilli is 28% to score, and Kent Johnson has 10 points in 10 games. Among our under-the-radar picks, Gabriel Landeskog, a third-line forward, has been dangerous with 2.8 expected goals in his last 10 games. They're players to watch, not locks.
